recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Do not rewrite the current R6 downloads page to match the old R4B/R5 package list; package-content issues found nearby should remain separate from this downloads-page text correction.
issue_request: FHIR-34429 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction for the R4B downloads page. It reported that the NPM package links used R4 package names and that core, examples, elements, and expansions all shared the same "all the conformance related resources" description, asking for the R5-style differentiated descriptions and R4B package URLs.
initial_application: The R5 downloads text had already been differentiated by b98b26f6cb50c11be16c313747ddb33bbea37ad1 before this Jira was filed, matching the issue's note that R5 was fixed. No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-34429 was found, but ba00883b28ad3217d530d9bbc4a1ed7adca788b6 on the R4B branch changed source/downloads.html from duplicated R4 package links/descriptions to R4B package links with distinct core, expansions, examples, elements, and corexml descriptions.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml includes source/downloads.html under Implementation Support, so the current downloads page is in build scope. The current source/downloads.html page lists R6 packages with distinct descriptions; later package-list work including FHIR-39010 and the R6 package update changed the package set without restoring the duplicate-description defect. Published R4B output at https://hl7.org/fhir/R4B/downloads.html also shows the requested r4b URLs and differentiated descriptions, and searches found no conflicting Zulip or Confluence evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current active source is already correct for the current build, and the historical R4B publication that the Jira targeted already contains the requested correction.
